name: Ang Chan I
extract:
Ang Chan I, also known as Chan Reachea the Great and Chao Ponhea Chan Reachea (Khmer: ចន្ទរាជា, Candarājā; 1486–1566) was a Cambodian king who reigned from 1516 to 1566. In his early years he was viceroy of the region of Phnom Penh and the eastern provinces, but was ousted by a pretender named Sdach Korn in 1512 and fled to Siam. He returned with a Siamese army in 1516 and was crowned king of Western Cambodia at Pursat after putting down several rebellions. A civil war with Korn ensued, leading to a number of battles involving firearms and cannons until Chan was finally victorious and crowned the king of all Cambodia.
Later, after the neighbouring Siamese invaded Cambodia twice, Chan regained the city of Longvek from the Siamese and built his new capital there, reigning peacefully until his death in 1566.
